He who has eaten such food, and has been fed and nourished with this sweetest and most delightful bread and the splendor of shining oil, will be turned into beauty and become most beautiful: not once, but repeated: 'exceedingly, exceedingly'; for the doubled adverb gives the speech this weight, that nothing further could be added to the greatness of the beauty.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And you advanced to a kingdom. — This is not found in the Seventy, who perhaps, translating the Scriptures at Alexandria from the Hebrew truth into the Greek language, feared to publish it, lest they seem to offend the king of Egypt by recording that a kingdom was owed to Jerusalem by God; although the learned prove that only the five books of Moses were translated by them. — After manifold adornment, then, after the crown, after the abundance of gold and silver, after the most beautiful garments and mantles, after incredible beauty, she advances to be queen, because she is the city of the great king, of whom it is written: O God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king's son; and in the Revelation of John Jerusalem is described as a bride adorned and arrayed for her husband; in the Psalms also it is said of her: The queen stood at your right hand in gilded clothing, surrounded with variety. But all that we say of Jerusalem, lest we dwell on each detail and the size of the books bring weariness to the readers, let us refer to the Church; for if Jerusalem, according to the Apostle, is our mother, and our mother is the Church, consequently Jerusalem is the Church, the mother of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven.
Against the Pelagians 2.25

In Ezekiel, God speaks to Jerusalem: "You were perfect through my beauty." And this is the meaning of the text: "You were not perfect through your own works or through your own knowledge and the boasting of your heart but through my beauty, which I had put on you freely through my mercy."
Commentary on Ezekiel

And your name went forth among the nations because of your fairness; for you were perfect in my beauty, which I set upon you, says the Lord God. (LXX: "And your name went out among the nations in your fairness; which was made complete in loveliness, which I set upon you, says the Lord God.") Symmachus translated this passage more clearly: And your name went forth among the nations; which was perfect because of my dignity, which I had set upon you, says the Lord God. And the sense is: 'By my benefits and my incredible bounty you came to the title of queen, so that the talk of all the nations spoke of you, and you were perfect, not by your own merits and virtues but by my liberality': Unless, indeed, the Lord builds the house, they have labored in vain who build it. Unless the Lord guards the city, he has watched in vain who guards it; for he who plants and he who waters is nothing, unless the Lord gives the increase, because: It is not of him who wills nor of him who runs, but of God who has mercy, so that, when we have done all things, we may say: We are unprofitable servants; we have done what we ought to do; not that the free choice of man is taken away by the beneficence of God, but that this very freedom ought to have the Lord as its helper.
Pastoral Rule, Part 4

But since often, when preaching is abundantly poured forth in fitting ways, the mind of the speaker is elevated in itself by a hidden delight in self-display, great care is needed that he may gnaw himself with the laceration of fear, lest he who recalls the diseases of others to health by remedies should himself swell through neglect of his own health; lest in helping others he desert himself, lest in lifting up others he fall. For to some the greatness of their virtue has often been the occasion of their perdition; causing them, while inordinately secure in confidence of strength, to die unexpectedly through negligence. For virtue strives with vices; the mind flatters itself with a certain delight in it; and it comes to pass that the soul of a well-doer casts aside the fear of its circumspection, and rests secure in self-confidence; and to it, now torpid, the cunning seducer enumerates all things that it has done well, and exalts it in swelling thoughts as though superexcellent beyond all beside.

Hence under the figure of Jerusalem the soul that is proud in virtue is reproved, when it is said, "Thou wert perfect in my comeliness which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord, and having confidence in thy beauty thou hast committed fornication in thy renown." For the mind is lifted up by confidence in its beauty, when, glad for the merits of its virtues, it glories within itself in security. But through this same confidence it is led to fornication; because, when the soul is deceived by its own thoughts, malignant spirits, which take possession of it, defile it through the seduction of innumerable vices. But it is to be noted that it is said, "Thou hast committed fornication in thy renown": for when the soul leaves off regard for the supernal ruler, it forthwith seeks its own praise, and begins to arrogate to itself all the good which it has received for shewing forth the praise of the giver; it desires to spread abroad the glory of its own reputation, and busies itself to become known as one to be admired of all.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And having confidence in your loveliness you fornicated in your name, and you laid out your fornication to everyone passing by, to become his. Great is the peril of trusting not in the clemency of God but in one's own beauty; and the more exalted anyone has been, the more he ought to fear lest he fall and fornicate in his own name. For the adverse powers despise ordinary foods and desire foreign nourishment; whence it is said of the devil: His foods are choice; he does not want to deceive just anyone: it is King Saul, who was chosen by the Lord, and Judas the apostle that he hastens to trip up. Let us not, therefore, trust in our own loveliness, nor think the liberality of God to be our own virtue, but rather let us hear: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what the coming day may bring forth, and in another place: Brothers, if a man is overtaken in any sin, you who are spiritual, perfect such a one in a spirit of meekness, considering yourself, lest you too be tempted; and let us not lay out, or pour out, our fornication to everyone passing by, so as to become not God's, in whom we believe, but his by whom we are defiled: he who receives all vices, and takes into his bosom the passing spirit of diverse sins, and spreads his feet for everyone passing by, he pours out his fornication, and begins to endure the dominion of him whose host he has become.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And taking some of your garments you made for yourself high places sewn together here and there; and you fornicated upon them, as has not been done nor will be. (LXX: "And you took some of your garments and made yourself idols sewn together; and you fornicated upon them, and you will not enter nor shall it be.") Symmachus translated this passage thus: And when you had taken some of your clothes, you made yourself many-colored high places; and you fornicated in them, things not done nor to be. For 'sewn together' and 'variegated' and 'high places' or 'idols', Aquila and Theodotion translated ἐμβολίσματα, which signifies 'diverse rags sewn together here and there' and 'an idol made like a plaster', as it were 'a πολύρραφον [much-stitched] garment'. 'I clothed you', he says, 'in variegated garments, and you were dressed in fine linen and many-threaded stuff and the variety of many forms; but you took your garments, with which you were gifted by my bounty, and made for yourself idols, or high places, which in Hebrew are called 'bamoth', a thing which never was done before nor will be done, that what you had received for adornment you should turn to the injury of the giver'. This can be understood of Jerusalem according to the letter thus: that she assigned all the precepts of the Law and her riches and the abundance of all things to idols, which no other nation has done or will do; for all the nations which from the beginning served idols are not guilty of so great a crime. But our Jerusalem, which means 'vision of peace', is torn by the heretics, when, plucking one testimony of the Scriptures or another from their proper places, they try to sew them onto places to which they cannot be fitted; to whom, as we read, it was also said above in this same prophet: Woe to those who sew pillows under every elbow of the hand, and make a covering over the head of every age, and the Lord, forbidding this to be done, says in the Gospel: No one puts a patch of rough cloth on an old garment; otherwise it takes away from its fullness, and a worse tear is made. Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; such are the Nazarenes, who try to fit the observance of the old Law to the grace of the Gospel, and all the heretics who strive to sew a testimony that fits one sense in its own place onto another, whereas the Lord's tunic, woven from the top throughout, cannot be torn, but, woven by the Holy Spirit, admits no tearing. But what is said according to the Seventy: And you will not enter nor will it be, signifies this: 'When you have made for yourself idols of perverse dogmas which you take for high places, and have fornicated upon them, believing in the things which you yourself have fashioned, you will not be able to enter the temple of God, and your images will have no substance nor will they exist forever', as the Apostle says: We know, indeed, that an idol is nothing in the world.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:2

The golden and silver vase, the censers, the cups and the rest of that kind we have in the holy Scriptures. But when we turn the meaning of Scripture into another that is contrary to the truth, we kindle the divine words and turn the things of God into other images.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And you took the vessels of your beauty, from my gold and from my silver which I gave you, and you made yourself male images, and you fornicated with them. According to the letter, the Lord commanded in the Law that there be made censers, bowls, a lampstand, the ark of the Covenant: all either of gold or gilded, and others of silver, all of which Jerusalem melted down and turned into idols of Bel or Baal, Chemosh, Ashtaroth and Milcom. According to the spiritual understanding, we make idols of the gold and silver of the holy Scriptures when we corrupt the grace of sense and eloquence by heretical depravity, and set our mouth in heaven, and our tongue passes through the earth; and male images is the name given to those in which every heresy fornicates, from the fact that each one thinks that what he worships and holds, which he has fashioned, is most robust and cannot be overthrown by any assault; these are the images which we have fashioned from our own heart and which are to be destroyed in the heavenly Jerusalem, of which the prophet foretells: O Lord, in your city you will scatter their image; for whoever is a man and has lost the name of God, it is said of him: Nevertheless man walks in an image; nevertheless he is disquieted in vain; but let us have one husband and venerate one image, which is the image of the invisible and almighty God.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:3

These various clothes and beautiful garments that God has bestowed on us, if we cut them up and rip them and surround them with false teaching to deceive human beings, there is no doubt that we are covering idols with different clothing.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:3
To me who preaches the gospel in the church, the devil always stretches out a noose, in order to confuse the whole church with my conduct.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:3
We do not imitate anyone, but if we want to imitate anyone, we should imitate Jesus Christ.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:5
Whoever is born in the teaching of heretics and has taken these principles for his own faith is a child of Jerusalem the fornicator and sinner.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And my oil and my perfume you set before them. And my bread (or, as the Seventy translated, my loaves which I gave you), fine flour, honey and oil with which I nourished you, you set in their sight for an odor of sweetness. The oil of which we spoke above, and the perfume or incense of which the psalmist cries out: Let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight, and the loaves of proposition which we are commanded to offer to God, the fine flour too, the purest sense of the Scriptures, and the honey which Jonathan tasted, and his eyes were opened and he was strengthened, wretched Jerusalem set in the sight of the idols — or before the male images —, that they might be for an odor of sweetness to them, things which by their nature are sweet and most delightful but, when they are offered to idols and false doctrines, are turned into bitterness.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And you took your many-colored garments, and covered them. 'The male images' is understood, so that she turned all the finery she had received for use into blasphemy. And we do this whenever we surround heretical depravity with prudence, temperance, fortitude, righteousness and all the virtues and, under their pretext, deceive all the simple, so that, seeing the honey of the virtues, they do not beware of the poisons of the vices.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And it came to pass, says the Lord God. And you took your sons and your daughters whom you bore to me, and you sacrificed them to them to be devoured — is your fornication a small thing, that you sacrificed my sons? —, you gave them up, consecrating them to them. And after all your abominations and fornications, you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and full of shame, trampled in your blood. (LXX: "And it came to pass, says Adonai the Lord. And you took your sons and your daughters whom you bore, and you sacrificed them to them for consumption, as though you had committed little fornication, and you killed your sons and gave them up when you offered them to them. This over and above all your fornication and your abominations; and you did not remember the day of your infancy, when you were naked and disgraced, you lived mingled in your blood.") That Jerusalem sacrificed her sons and daughters to idols — the sons and daughters of whom it is written: Sons I have begotten and exalted, but they have despised me — holy Scripture records: They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons, and again: They poured out innocent blood, the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed to the carved images of Canaan. Now according to the Hebrew he calls them 'his own' — for he himself had said of them: Israel is my firstborn son — or, according to the Seventy, 'yours', those whom you begot of fornication. And in that place where we have put: And you gave them up, consecrating them to them, for which the Seventy translated: And you gave them up for appeasing (or for expiating), Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion put: You carried them across and led them through, by which the heathens, through fire, either carry their sons across while they are little or compel them, when grown, to pass through. 'Although you have done these things so, you did not remember your infancy, when I took you up, spattered with blood, and washed you, and — after the many things which the prophetic discourse has related — joined you to myself'. Our Jerusalem too, if she has been tripped up by heretical deceit, takes her sons who are stronger in faith and her daughters who do not have such great strength of faith — or certainly the sons who know every mystical thing, the daughters who follow the simple history — and hands them over to demons to be devoured, and while she kills them she believes that she is giving life and appeasing the images, which are glutted with their slaughter. And what is said according to the Seventy: This is over and above all your fornication and your abominations, signifies that the teaching of the heretics is worse than all sins and fornications, for it makes the sons of God sons of demons, nay rather it kills those whom she had either begotten for God with much labor or had made her own sons, those whom she begot in fornication.
SERMON ON THE MOUNT 1:12.36

By the name of such adulterers we are to understand every kind of carnal and lustful concupiscence. Indeed, since the Scriptures so constantly give to idolatry the name of fornication, and since the apostle Paul calls avarice idolatry, who can doubt that every evil concupiscence may be rightly called fornication?
SERMON ON THE MOUNT 1:12.36
When the soul disregards the higher law by which it is governed and prostitutes itself as though for a price, then it corrupts itself.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:6
Their bodies are corrupted, and the soul is wounded.
HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 43:1

For what saith He? "An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign." Now what He saith is to this effect: What marvel if ye behave so to me who have been hitherto unknown to you when even to the Father, of whom ye have had so much experience, ye have done the very same? forsaking Him, ye have run unto the devils, drawing to yourselves wicked lovers. With this Ezekiel too was continually upbraiding them.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And it happened after all your wickedness, woe, woe to you, says the Lord God, and you built yourself a brothel, and you made yourself a place of prostitution in all the streets; at every head of the way you built the sign of your prostitution, and you made your beauty abominable, and you parted your feet to every passer-by, and you multiplied your fornications. And you committed fornication with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors, of great flesh, and you multiplied your fornication to provoke me. (LXX: "And it came to pass after all your wickednesses, ※ woe, woe to you, ⁚ says Adonai the Lord, and you built yourself a dwelling of fornication, and you made yourself prostitution in every street, and at the beginning of every way you built your fornications, and you corrupted your beauty, and you spread your legs to every passer-by, and you multiplied your fornication. And you committed fornication with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors, who are of great flesh, and you committed fornication manifoldly to provoke me to anger.") This, which is said a second time: Woe, woe to you, the common edition does not have, but it was added from the translation of Theodotion; and again, where we said: And you built yourself a brothel, for which the Seventy translated: And you built yourself a dwelling of fornication, Symmachus and Theodotion translated πορνεῖον [brothel], while Aquila, wishing to express the ἐτυμολογίαν [etymology] of the Hebrew word 'gob', put βόθυνον, which we could call 'a pit', to signify a den of vice and a dug-out, dark cave in which the lust of prostitutes has its haunt; and what follows: And you made yourself a place of prostitution in all the streets, for which the Seventy said ἔκθεμα [a thing set out for show], has in the Hebrew 'rama', and Aquila as well as Symmachus and Theodotion translated it 'high place' or 'lofty'; and then in what follows it is also written: At every head of the way you built the sign of your prostitution — for 'sign' and 'fornication' the Hebrew again has 'rama', which we have translated either 'place of prostitution' or 'sign', since among the Hebrews it is a single word —, and this is set up, or is made rather high, so that the place of fornication may be seen from afar by those who wish to fornicate and there may be no need to search for it.
Commentary on Ezekiel

To our Jerusalem too, whether the Church or the souls of believers, if they have been negligent and have lain open to all vices, a twofold word of cursing is addressed, so that they hear: Woe, woe to you, says the Lord God, according to what is written in the Revelation of John: Woe upon all the inhabitants of the earth. For if a holy man says: I am a stranger and a sojourner, as all my fathers were, why should not the sinner be said to be an inhabitant of the earth?
Commentary on Ezekiel

Now he builds himself a brothel who sins with complete brazenness of brow, according to what is written: The sinner, when he has come into the depth of impiety, despises. And he raises a very high place in all the streets: For wide and spacious is the way that leads to death.
Commentary on Ezekiel

What we have said once, and again and again, let it suffice to have said for good: that under the person of a woman who commits fornication after her husband's many benefits, the fornication of Jerusalem is described: how she withdrew from God and was joined to idols and was not content with hidden fornication, but built herself a brothel and in every way set up a sign for passers-by — that they might come to the harlot and sate their lust, not so much their own as hers who spread her legs to every passer-by —, and disfigured the greatness of her beauty by the greatness of her fornication; and among other things she prostrated herself to the Egyptians too, her neighbors, out of love for great flesh, and, to display every kind of foulness, was disfigured by a manifold kind of filth.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:7
Possessing these things, she is of great beauty, but she is corrupted by the divisions of heretics and foreign religious systems.
LETTER 22.6

She will sit by the waters of loneliness, her pitcher laid aside, and open her legs to every one who passes by and be polluted to the crown of her head. It would have been better for her to have submitted to the yoke of marriage, to have walked in level places, than to aspire to loftier heights and fall into the depths of hell.
LETTER 79.10

A noble alternative only to be embraced in preference to Satan! In the old days even Jerusalem went whoring and opened her legs to everyone that passed by. It was in Egypt that she was first deflowered and there that her teats were bruised.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And he builds at every head of the way, so as to leave no kind of sin untried, but, imitating the harlot of Proverbs, openly in the streets and at the corners of the streets he invites the foolish young men passing by to his embraces, and defiles the beauty of the soul which he received as a gift from God the creator.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And all his ways are full of foulness, and to all the thoughts that supply the incitements of vices he opens his heart and spreads his legs, and he commits fornication with the Egyptians his neighbors, whose examples he follows, namely the heathens, who glory in their foulnesses, and he is so wicked as to surpass even them in foulness. And all this he does to provoke God to anger. Now the Egyptians are said to be of great flesh, either because of the greatness of their foulness or because of the deformity of their sins: hence the holy man is said to be of little flesh, which in him decreases daily and is thinned away by the virtues, so that it is no longer called flesh but spirit; and he says in the psalm: My soul has thirsted for you, O God, how manifoldly my flesh for you (or, as some copies have, how my flesh has been consumed), in a desert land, pathless and waterless, so in the holy place I have appeared to you; for this reason the Corinthian fornicator too is handed over: For the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved; of this flesh it is written: All flesh is grass, and all its glory like the flower of grass; the grass has withered and the flower has fallen; but the word of the Lord abides forever, of which the Apostle also spoke: Flesh and blood shall not possess the kingdom of God, and in Genesis God says: My spirit shall not remain in these men, because they are flesh, and to believers it is said: Those who are in the flesh cannot appease God. But you are not in the flesh but in the spirit; but the flesh of the saints is another, of which it is written: All flesh shall see the salvation of God.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:8
You see that she is handed over to the souls of strangers, she who is unworthy to practice the law and the words of God.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Now no one doubts that Palestine is a neighbor of Egypt, since the Lord says to Abraham: I will give you all the land, from the river of Egypt to the great river Euphrates, so that on one side it has the Egyptians, on the other the Assyrians, with whom too she is said further on to have committed fornication; and the fornication of Jerusalem with the Egyptians is the imitation of their idolatry.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Behold, I will stretch out my hand over you, and I will take away your justification, and I will give you up in the souls of those who hate you, of the Palestinian daughters, who blush at your wicked way. (LXX: "But if I stretch out my hand over you, and I will take away your ordinances, and I will give you into the souls of those who hate you, of the daughters of the foreigners, who made you turn aside from your way." And what follows: Ἠσέβησας, that is: You acted impiously, is fitted according to the Seventy to the following section, according to the others it is the end of the preceding one.) Now the Lord stretches out his hand over Jerusalem, to correct her in her sinning and to take away her ordinances, which, as long as she kept the precepts of God, were called the ordinances of the Lord, but when she worshiped idols and exchanged religion for impiety, are called her ordinances — which is to be understood not only of the law and the ceremonies, but also of the sabbaths and the feast days and the new moons: for when he gives the law he says: My sabbaths and: My feast days, but when they withdrew from God, it is said to them: Your new moons and sabbaths and the great day I will not receive; your fasting and rest and your solemnities my soul has hated; which is written of the people as well: for those who were formerly called the people of God, after they withdrew from the Lord, it is said of them to Moses: Your people have sinned, whom you led out of the land of Egypt —. What is here called the stretching out of the hand is elsewhere called lifting up or visitation: for when God does not rebuke the sinner, he draws back his hand, but if he sins and begins to sicken in the law of God, a visitation is sent to him, according to what is sung in the Psalms: If his sons forsake my law and do not walk in my judgments, I will visit their iniquities with the rod, and in this prophet it is written: The land, if it sins against me so as to commit an offense, I will stretch out my hand over it, and I will break the staff of its bread, and the rest; in which we ask what difference there is between the stretching out of the hand and the sending of it: for the devil says to the Lord: Send your hand, and touch all that he has; unless he blesses you to your face, and it seems to me that the hand is sent for the testing of those to whom it is sent, but stretched out for the punishment of those who deserve torments; and not only the stretching out and the sending, but also the spreading out of the hand of God is spoken of, as Isaiah proclaims in the person of the Lord: All day long I have spread out my hands to a people unbelieving and contradicting; the saints too are related to lift up their hands, as Scripture says: The lifting up of my hands an evening sacrifice. Now since the ordinances of God have been taken away from the people of the Jews, let us ask them what observance of the law they have: victims they cannot offer, since the temple has been taken away and overthrown, nor can the stoning of adulteresses and of the other crimes, granted by the law, be carried out, nor the rest of the land in the year of remission, and the other things of this kind; and she is given into the souls of those who hate her, of the Palestinian daughters, when she is handed over to the Palestinians, whom the Seventy indiscriminately call 'foreigners', by which we may understand the cities or towns of Palestine. Our Jerusalem too, if we pass over the ceremonies of God, and his hand has been stretched out over us, and, the observance of the whole law having been taken away, she will be handed over to the daughters of Palestine and not to the sons; for we are not handed over first to the heavier punishments but, according to the quality of our sins, to the lesser ones, so that, chastised in the smaller, we may escape the greater torments of tortures. 'Philistim', that is 'Palaestini' [Palestinians], with the first part of the letters changed, means 'falling by the cup — or by the making —', by which it is signified that we are to be handed over to the adverse powers, which have drunk from the cup of Babylon and have fallen, and whose works are perverse; and so great will be the chastisement and disgrace of wretched Jerusalem that even the adverse powers themselves blush at the greatness of our sins. What we have translated, following Symmachus, 'wicked', Theodotion put as the Hebrew word itself, 'zemma'. And since the ceremonies of God have been taken away from the people of the Jews, the giving of the law passes over to us together with the priesthood, as Scripture says: Appoint, O Lord, a lawgiver over them, and in another place: Set me a law, O Lord, in your way.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:9

When God makes covenants with us and we consent to them, we are blessed. But when we prostitute ourselves to the spirits of evil, then we turn the covenants of God into the land of Canaan, and we make a pact with her.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And you committed fornication with the sons of the Assyrians, because you had not yet been filled; and after you committed fornication, not even so were you satisfied. And you multiplied your fornication in the land of Canaan with the Chaldeans, and not even so were you satisfied. (LXX: "And you acted impiously, and you committed fornication with the sons of Assyria, and not even so were you satisfied; and you committed fornication, and you were not filled. And you multiplied your covenants toward the land of Canaan of the Chaldeans, and not even in these were you filled.") Above it was written that Jerusalem committed fornication with the sons of Egypt her neighbors, who are of great flesh; here the other neighborhood, that of the Assyrians, is indicated; and therefore they are handed over to both nations: because they venerated the images of both, and, entering Chaldea, which is the land of Canaan, they took on in exchange the errors of those to whose rule they were subject. According to tropology we often pass from some sins to others; and when we have not done penance for our former crimes, we add offense to offenses and are sated by no error, but as with a long rope and the strap of a heifer's yoke we drag along our sins and our covenant, or we multiply fornication in the land of 'Chanaan' [Canaan], which means 'as it were a tossing', with the Chaldeans, who themselves also sound to us 'as it were demons'; and we always have our footprints in the sand and can never say: He has set my feet upon a rock; and we are subjected to the depravities of the heretics, who have the likeness of demons, or to the demons themselves, of whom Paul writes: Our fight is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers of these darknesses, against the spiritual things of wickedness in the heavenly places.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:10

As the law is not made for the just but for the lawless and those who are not subjected to God, so the teaching that warns us away from fornication does not become chaste but is for the lawless and the fornicators and the disobedient.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 7:10
If you understand fornication of the flesh and the soul and the spirit, and if you see someone fornicating in them, you will also see Jerusalem fornicating herself three times.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 8:1
There is no doubt that the word of the orator provokes the hero to worse things when a heretic builds up his hero in the perversions of heresy by what he says.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 8:1
Those who have not completely gone away from religion but are conquered by sin and who want their sin to be hidden behave exactly like a prostitute who has been insulted.
Commentary on Ezekiel

In what shall I cleanse your heart, says the Lord God, when you do all these works of a harlot and wanton woman? For you have built your brothel at the head of every way, and you have made your high place in every street; nor have you become like a harlot who increases her price by disdain. (LXX: "What shall I do to your heart, says Adonai the Lord, when you have done all these works of a fornicating and shameless woman? ÷ and you committed fornication threefold in your daughters ⁚ when you built your brothel at the beginning of every way, and made your base in every street; and you were not like a harlot gathering wages.") And what the Seventy said: And you committed fornication threefold in your daughters, is not found in the Hebrew, nor did any of the other translators put it. Now God says all these things to Jerusalem Ἐπαπορητικῶς [as one at a loss], because he cannot find the remedy by which he might heal her, sick and half dead, according to what Isaiah writes: What is there that I ought to have done further for my vineyard, and have not done for it?, and Hosea: What shall I do to you, Ephraim? What shall I do to you, Judah? Your mercy is like a morning cloud, and like the dew passing away early.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And this which, as we said above, is not found in the Hebrew: You committed fornication threefold in your daughters, is said either to Jerusalem according to the letter: that she committed fornication in every way in her towns and villages, and no corner or street remained where she did not set up the signs of idolatry; or to the Church and to the believers who were deceived: who did not heed that word of the Apostle: May the God of peace himself sanctify you in all things, and may your spirit and soul and body be kept whole without complaint at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but committed fornication in every way, both in body and in spirit and in soul. We read in Proverbs: But you, describe them threefold, that you may answer words of truth which are proposed to you, and we are commanded to understand the utterances of truth, that is, the holy Scriptures, threefold: first, according to the letter; second, in a middle way, through tropology; third, more loftily, so that we may know all mystical things. According to the letter is this: Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day, and: Do not murmur, as some of them murmured, and perished by the destroyer; in the middle way and according to tropology, when we withdraw from the letter and climb a little to higher things, as the Apostle says: It is written: You shall not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treads out the grain, and immediately there follows: Is it for oxen that God cares? Or did he speak surely for our sake?; but the last, that is, the third, sublime and sacred understanding, according to that word of the same Apostle: For this reason a man shall leave father and mother and shall cleave to his wife. This mystery is great; but I speak in Christ and in the Church. Now the daughters of the fornicating Church are the souls of those who first believed and afterwards were deceived into heresy, whose guilt is referred back to the mother.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 8:2
Ecclesiastics who are leaders in the church build the house of God, the church, in their own way of life as well as those of their faithful, and their work is the building of God.
Commentary on Ezekiel

'For your idolatry was committed not in secret but with full license, so that at all the beginnings of the ways and at the crossroads you set up altars, and made your base, or your high place, of which we spoke above, in every street; nor did you imitate the cunning harlots, who are accustomed to increase the price of lust by difficulty and thereby provoke their lovers the more to madness — according to the Seventy: You were not like a harlot gathering wages —, but you gave what you ought to have received, so that not even in this, that you committed fornication and followed demons, were you protected by their help, but, oppressed by various captivities, you felt your calamities'. Which indeed can also be referred to every Christian soul that, having deserted the worship of God, has given itself up to vices and luxury and, having followed the worldly life, has not fared happily even in it, but has both lost the riches of religion and not received the riches of the world, nor was there any difficulty in debauching her, but she thrust herself upon your lovers. There is also another, spiritual fornication, when, deserting the Church, we are joined to heretics and build our brothel at the head of every way, the ways of which the divine word commands: Stand in the ways and seek the everlasting paths of the Lord, and see which is the good way, and walk in it, namely the books of Moses, of Joshua, of Judges and of Kings, and Isaiah and Jeremiah and the other prophets. He builds his brothel at all the beginnings of the ways who, for the perversity of his doctrine, wickedly abuses the testimonies of the Scriptures and says: 'Thus says Isaiah': 'Thus said Hosea': 'Thus spoke Moses' and: 'Thus Daniel'; and fittingly he places his brothel not in the middle of the ways nor at the ends of the ways, but at the beginning: for if he had come to the knowledge and the depths of the divine books, he could not go astray. His high place too, or base, he makes in every street, giving himself up to the wantonness and vices of heathens and impious men, even among the heretics themselves, when she has been defiled by them, having no favor but lying open to contempt, because she easily lost her former chastity of faith.
Letter 3: Against the Treatise of the Novatians

Your cruelty is a false faith. An heretical congregation is an adulteress woman; for the Catholic hath never from the beginning left the couch and the chamber of her Spouse, nor gone after other and strange lovers. Ye have painted a divorced form in new colours, ye have withdrawn your couch from the old wedlock, ye have left the body of a mother, the wife of One Husband, decking yourselves out with new arts of pleasing, new allurements of corruption.
Commentary on Ezekiel

But as an adulterous woman who brings in strangers over her husband. To all harlots wages are given, but you have given wages to all your lovers, and you made gifts to them that they might come in to you from every side to commit fornication with you. And it has happened in you contrary to the custom of women in your fornications, and after you there will be no fornication; for in that you gave wages and did not receive wages, the contrary has happened in you. (LXX: "An adulterous woman ÷ like you ⁚ receiving wages from her husband. To all who committed fornication with her she gave wages, and you gave wages to all your lovers, and you loaded them that they might come to you round about in your fornication. And there happened in you a perverse thing against women in your fornication, and after you they have not committed fornication; in that you gave wages and wages were not given to you, there also happened in you a perverse thing.") This which is written in the Seventy: Like you, is not found in the Hebrew; and it disturbs the order of the reading, and raises no small question: what woman, and like whom she is, since Jerusalem herself is said to be the adulterous woman. Jerusalem, then, took the abundance of all things with which she had been endowed by her husband's liberality, and gave it to strangers, namely to demons and idols, according to what is written in Hosea: And this I did not know, that I gave her wheat and wine and oil, and multiplied silver for her; but she made silver and golden Baalim, whence, angered, he at once adds: Therefore I will turn back, and take away my wheat in its season and my wine in its season; and I will take away my garments and my linens, so that I may no longer cover her disgrace; and now I will uncover her disgrace in the sight of her lovers, and no one shall rescue her from my hand.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Whatever we have said of Jerusalem, refer also to the Church and to the souls of believers, who give their marriage gifts — namely gold in understanding and silver in speech and the garments by which our foulness and disgrace are veiled — to their lovers, either to the contrary powers or to the teachers of perverse doctrines, when they assert that luxury does no harm, and that indiscriminate lust, according to the genitals of the body, demands intercourse by natural law, that all foods are to be used without distinction, since they were made for this, to be eaten, that prudence is necessary only in so far as it profits oneself, and that righteousness has no place, for if it prevailed one would have to beg, and other things of this kind; receiving which, wretched Jerusalem, in whom there ought to have been a vision of peace, turned the sharpness of her intellect and the charm of her eloquence to foulness; and for her lovers she went forth against her husband adorned with those ornaments with which she had been adorned by her husband, to the abuse of the good. And what follows: And you made gifts to them that they might come in to you from every side to commit fornication with you, signifies every kind of sin, so that she is not content with one offense, but endures a hunger for sinning and, against the laws of nature, defiled in all her members, is polluted even to the crown of her head.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 8:3
The husband of the soul is the word of God, a spouse truly loving, who has given her chastity, justice and all the other gifts.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And whereas all fornicating women are accustomed to receive wages from their lovers, Jerusalem did the contrary, giving rather than receiving; and to show the lavishness of her wages: She loaded them, he says, that they might come to her round about, lest there be any neighbor who was not mingled in her disgrace.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And indeed Jerusalem surpassed the other harlots in this too, that she not only gave her own things, which she had acquired by labor in the practice of foulness, but also bestowed her marriage gifts on her lovers and debauchers. And so great was the adulteress's exposure to every magnitude of foulness that she is ranked above not only present but also future harlots; hence we too translated according to Symmachus: 'And after you there will be no fornication; for in comparison with you every fornication from now on will be reckoned lighter'.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Therefore, harlot, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Because your bronze has been poured out, and your disgrace has been uncovered in your fornication over your lovers, and over the idols of your abominations in the blood of your sons whom you gave to them, behold, I will gather all your lovers with whom you mingled, and all whom you loved, together with all whom you hated; and I will gather them against you from every side, and I will lay bare your disgrace before them, and they will see all your foulness. And I will judge you with the judgments of adulteresses and of those who shed blood, and I will give you into the blood of fury and jealousy. And I will give you into their hands, and they will destroy your brothel, and they will demolish your place of prostitution, and they will strip you of your garments, and they will take away the vessels of your beauty; and they will leave you naked, and full of disgrace. And they will bring a multitude upon you, and they will stone you with stones, and they will cut you down with their swords. And they will burn your houses with fire, and they will execute judgments upon you in the eyes of very many women; and you will cease to commit fornication, and you will no longer give wages. And my indignation will rest in you, and my jealousy will be taken away from you; and I will be quiet, and will be angry no more. Because you did not remember the days of your youth, and provoked me in all these things, therefore I too have given your ways upon your head, says the Lord God, and I have not done according to your crimes in all your abominations. (LXX: "Therefore, harlot, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Because you poured out your bronze, and your disgrace will be uncovered in your fornication to all your lovers, and into all the thoughts of your iniquities and in the blood of your sons whom you gave to them, therefore behold, I will gather against you all your lovers with whom you mingled, and all whom you loved together with all whom you hated; and I will gather them against you round about, and I will uncover your wickednesses to them, and all will see your disgrace. And I will take vengeance on you with the vengeance of adulteresses and of those who shed blood, and I will set you in the blood of fury and jealousy. And I will deliver you into their hands, and they will dig under your brothel, and they will destroy your base, and they will strip you of your garments, and they will take away the vessels of your glorying; and they will leave you naked, and full of disgrace. And they will bring a multitude upon you, and they will stone you with stones and cut you down with their swords. And they will set fire to your houses, and they will execute vengeances upon you before very many women; and I will turn you away from fornication, and you will no longer give wages. And I will send my fury upon you, and my jealousy will be taken away from you; and I will rest, and I will no longer be anxious. Because you did not remember the day of your infancy, and you grieved me in all these things, I too, behold, will give your ways upon your head, says Adonai the Lord, and thus you have done iniquity above all your iniquities.") Let us first lay the foundations of the history. 'Because you have done these things and those which the preceding discourse has set out, therefore hear, harlot, what you have done and what you are going to suffer: You poured out your bronze, which you had received from me, and gave to your lovers the wages which you ought to have received, and you killed your sons, so that, in offering them to idols, you have proved to be not only an adulteress but also a parricide. Therefore I will gather against you all your lovers with whom you committed fornication, both those whom you loved and those whom you hated, and I will strip you by the law of adulteresses, so that all may see your foulness and the genitals for whose sake they were formerly carried away by the madness of love'. Now all these things, through the μεταφορὰν [metaphor] of an adulterous and murderous woman who not only committed fornication against her husband but also killed her sons, are said to Jerusalem: both that all the nations are to be gathered against her, whose idols she worshiped and into whose worship she turned all the gifts of God, and that the temple of Baal is to be destroyed, and the altars of the whole city overthrown by fire, and nothing is to remain in her; and that, just as all are accustomed to throw stones at an adulteress and to slaughter a harlot, so that she is killed by the wounds of each one, in such a way that all women see the punishment of the fornicatress, so Jerusalem is to be abandoned in the sight of the other cities round about and of all the nations; and that this is done so that she may cease to commit fornication and may no longer give wages to her lovers, and so that the indignation of God may rest and he may not be angry with her whom he has ceased to love; from which we perceive that it is a great mark of displeasure to be in no way an object of God's care, but for a man to be left to his crimes and sins. My jealousy, he says, will be taken away from you; and I will be quiet, and will be angry no more, as with one estranged, who has withdrawn from me and whom I have handed over to everlasting nakedness — but if Jerusalem suffered this because she committed fornication with idols, what do we think she will suffer when she has slaughtered the Son of God? —.
Commentary on Ezekiel

According to tropology, every soul has received spiritual money from God, according to that passage of the Gospel which is told in the parables of the five, the two and the one talents, and of the ten servants receiving a mina each, who, when they have acted negligently, will become debtors of fifty denarii and of five hundred; and for this reason, in the presence of the lovers, whom we understand to be the demons and the contrary powers, the disgrace of Jerusalem is uncovered, either on the day of judgment or in the time of penance, when they are rebuked; and at first, indeed, God almighty alone discerns hidden things, as the word of the Gospel says: And the Father who sees in secret, and in another place: God searching hearts and reins, and in the volume of Kings: You alone know the hearts of all men; but when there has been fulfilled: There is nothing hidden that will not be made manifest and covered that will not be revealed, and in another place: Do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and make manifest the counsels of hearts, and then each one will have praise from God, and when the time of rebuke has come, then that word of Hosea is fulfilled: Now their thoughts have surrounded them, and in another place: Their thoughts among themselves accusing or else defending, on the day when God judges the secrets of men, and again: Behold the man, and his works before his face. And those who formerly committed fornication with her will see all her foulness, and God will give her into the blood of fury and jealousy; for the fury of a husband against an adulterous wife is full, and can be redeemed by no price. The blood of the sons, moreover, can be understood thus, that we call the sons of Jerusalem λογισμούς καλούς, that is, 'good thoughts', which have been implanted in men by God, and which the adulteress killed when she turned aside to evil works. It also profits Jerusalem that her brothel should be dug under and every seedbed of fornication destroyed: for when this has been done, she will no longer give wages, and the indignation of God will rest, and he will in no way be jealous over her, being secure about her chastity; that is, according to those who take what is said in a good sense. Others, however, as we said above, refer it to the contrary sense, so that it belongs to God's great anger not to be angry with them, once he has despised the fornicatress and despaired of her salvation; but if the heretics who do not receive the Old Testament should, according to the edition of the Seventy, find fault in this place with what is said: And you grieved me in all these things, on the ground that God not only admits anger but is also subject to grief and sadness, let us ask them how they accept this, which is certainly a command of the good God: Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed in the day of redemption; for whatever they say in defense of that testimony, we shall apply in satisfaction of the present passage.
HOMILIES ON EXODUS 8

But if, chastised, you do not come to your senses, if, rebuked, you are not amended, if, scourged, you despise it, know that, if you have so far advanced in sinning, his jealousy will depart from you, and that will be said to you which through the prophet Ezekiel is said to Jerusalem: "therefore my jealousy shall depart from you, and I will be angry over you no more".
LETTER 68

It is when God shows no anger to sinners that his anger is great. So in the case of Ezekiel he said to Jerusalem, "Now I shall not be angry with you, my jealousy has left you." … So that I may not go too far and overrun the length of a letter by piling up instances from the Old Testament, I shall tell you a brief story that happened in the days of my childhood. When the blessed Antony was summoned by Athanasius, bishop of Alexandria, to the city of Alexandria to confute heretics, and Didymus, a most learned and blessed man, had a meeting with him, they had a discussion about the holy Scriptures. Antony admired the other's brain and praised his mental sharpness. Then he asked, "I imagine that your blindness does not depress you?" Didymus in his shame said nothing. But when Antony asked a second and third time, he finally succeeded in eliciting from Didymus a simple expression of grief. Antony said to him, "I am surprised at a wise man grieving at the loss of what ants, flies and gnats have rather than rejoicing at having what only the saints and apostles have deserved to get." From this you can realize that it is much better to see with the spirit than with the flesh and to possess the eyes that the mote of sin cannot enter.
Commentary on Ezekiel

'And all these things', he says, 'you have done, forgetful of former benefits, and you have provoked me to anger, or grieved me, whom you ought to have provoked to joy by good works. Therefore I too have rendered your works upon your head. And although I overthrew you, O adulteress, yet I will exercise less of my anger on you than you deserved'; so that in this too the divine clemency may be shown, that the sins are greater than the punishments.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Behold, everyone who speaks a common proverb will take it up against you, saying: As the mother, so also her daughter. You are the daughter of your mother, who cast off her husband and her sons; and you are the sister of your sisters, who cast off their husbands and their sons. (LXX: "These are all the things which they said against you in a parable, saying: As the mother, also the daughter. You are the daughter of your mother, who leaves her husband and her sons, and sisters of your sisters, who left their husbands and their sons.") After the κατάλογον [catalogue] of the vices and of the chastisement of Jerusalem, by which she is drawn back to salvation, there is also applied a proverb worn by the common speech of the people, or, as the Seventy translated, a 'parable': Such as the mother, such also the daughter.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:1

Where there are sins, where there are multitudes of people, there are schisms, there are heresies, there are dissensions. But where there is virtue, there is unity, union, from which the single heart and spirit of all believers were made.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:1
To put it more clearly, the origin of all evils is the multitude, but the origin of good things is to retire from the crowd and to confine oneself to the solitary life.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 1:9
As the Father and Son are one, so those who have one Spirit are brought together in unity.
Commentary on Ezekiel

The heretics who nevertheless accept the Old Testament are accustomed to understand three natures from this passage: spiritual, animal and earthly, and they refer the spiritual to Jerusalem, the animal to Samaria, the earthly to Sodom; let us briefly ask them how three natures, spiritual, animal and earthly, which are certainly different from one another, are said to have one mother and one father — which does not agree with their fiction —, and how the animal and the earthly nature, according to this same prophet, are restored to their ancient state, that is, to the spiritual — which is itself also contrary to their reasonings —. Now that Samaria is to be understood of the heresies is proved both in the prophet Hosea and in many other places, and especially by that testimony: Woe to those who despise Zion and who trust in the mountain of Samaria; they have gathered as a vintage the chiefs of the nations; for all heretics despise 'Sion' [Zion], which means 'watchtower' and is referred to the Church, and they trust in the mountain of Samaria, namely in the pride of perverse doctrines which they think sublime, and through these frauds of preaching they gather as a vintage and lay waste the chiefs of the nations, so that, by the marvel of their doctrines, they draw all the powerful among the Gentiles into heretical error.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Now the mother of Jerusalem, as is written both above and in what follows, is called 'chethaea' [Hittite], and it means 'raving' or 'turning into madness', by which are shown the incitements of this world, which lead the captive soul to destruction and separate her from her husband — there is no doubt that by him the word of God and doctrine are meant —; and she is the sister of her sisters, who, as we shall read a little later, are called Sodom and Samaria, of whom the one signifies the life and luxury of the Gentiles, the other the snares of the heretics. Furthermore, what is read in the Seventy: Sisters of your sisters, who repulsed their husbands and their sons, makes no sense — for what other sisters did Sodom and Samaria have, who are the sisters of Jerusalem? And this too must be asked, what husbands Sodom and Samaria sent away and what sons they cast off —, unless perhaps we can say this: that the feet of those who go astray always waver, and theirs are not the solid footsteps that properly belong to the truth, but they run hither and thither and are carried about by every wind of doctrine, while they pass from falsehood to another falsehood and, when they have realized that they toiled in vain over the first, cross over to the second and the third.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Your mother a Hittite, and your father an Amorite. And your greater sister is Samaria, she — and her daughters — who dwells at your left hand; but your sister lesser than you, who dwells at your right hand, is Sodom and her daughters. But you have not walked in their ways, nor done a little less according to their crimes; you have done things almost more wicked than they in all your ways. (LXX: "Your mother a Hittite, and your father an Amorite. Your elder sister is Samaria, she — and her daughters — who dwells on your left; and your sister younger than you, who dwells on your right, is Sodom and her daughters. And not even so did you walk in their ways, nor did you act a little less according to her iniquities; and you surpassed them in all your ways.") Above he had said: Your father an Amorite and your mother a Hittite; here, with the order and the number changed: Your mother a Hittite and your father an Amorite. For when crimes have advanced, they are split into parts, and, unity forsaken, they advance into a crowd and a multitude, which cannot climb to the mountains with Jesus.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:1
Virtue makes me to have Christ as my brother, so that I may be both good and well-mannered.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:1
What are these two sisters of Jerusalem the sinner? Schism and division of the people created Samaria.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:1
This is to despise Zion and to trust in the mountain of Samaria. For if we ecclesiastics sin, heretics are certainly not strangers to us in the perversion of their teaching.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Now that Samaria and Sodom are the sisters of Jerusalem, of whom one is on the left and the other on the right, you will confirm even according to the bodily understanding, if you look toward the east from the temple of Jerusalem; and Samaria is called greater because she sinned first and was led into captivity by the Assyrians, and Sodom lesser and younger, which is referred to the crowd of the Gentiles; otherwise, at that time Sodom did not exist, for before we read of Jerusalem in the Scriptures, it had been destroyed by divine fire together with Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And Jerusalem, in the middle between the two sisters, which by another name is called Judah, was led by the Chaldeans into Babylon, and Jerusalem sinned far more wickedly than Samaria and Sodom, worshiping in the temple the idol of Jealousy and afterwards killing the Son of God. Furthermore, according to tropology, Samaria and Sodom, that is, the heretics and the heathens, often commit lighter things than those who are reckoned to be Jerusalem, that is, the churchmen; hence it is said to the Corinthians, who believed indeed in Christ but were weighed down by evil works: Fornication is actually heard of among you; and such fornication as is not even among the Gentiles, so that someone has his father's wife, and the rest.
Commentary on Ezekiel

As I live, says the Lord God, Sodom your sister, she and her daughters, has not done as you and your daughters have done. Behold, this was the iniquity of Sodom your sister: pride, fullness of bread and abundance, and the idleness of her and of her daughters, and they did not stretch out a hand to the needy and the poor; and they were lifted up and committed abominations before me, and I took them away as you saw. And Samaria did not commit half of your sins; but you have surpassed her by your crimes, and you have justified your sisters in all your abominations which you have wrought. (LXX: "As I live, says Adonai the Lord, if Sodom your sister has done, she and her daughters, as you and your daughters have done. Nevertheless the iniquity of Sodom your sister was pride in fullness of breads and in abundance. She abounded in delights, she and her daughters ÷ this she had, she and her daughters ⁚ and she did not take hold of the hand of the poor and needy; and they gloried magnificently and committed iniquities in my sight, and I took them away as you saw. And Samaria did not commit half of your sins; and you multiplied your iniquities beyond them, and you justified your sisters in all your iniquities which you have wrought.") What the Seventy put: This she had, she and her daughters, is not found in the Hebrew. In the Old Testament the oath of God is: As I live, says the Lord God, but in the New: Amen, amen I say to you; but if this is common with others: The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob; he is not the God of the dead, but of the living, and in another place: I will please the Lord in the land of the living, we ask by what reason God claims a common word as properly his own; but just as a good tree is spoken of, and a good man, and a good shepherd, and a good servant — yet no one is absolutely good but the one God —, so, although the angels and the other powers, and also the patriarchs and prophets and apostles, are living, in comparison with God almighty they are called dead: Who is the man who shall live and not see death?; hence the apostle Paul too says of God: Who alone, he says, has immortality, and dwells in light inaccessible, and of the fountain of the living: Our life, he says, is hidden with Christ in God.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:2
To know that sins are unequal you only have to look at the teaching of the Scriptures, which will leave you in no doubt.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:2

What then is the sin most great of all sins? It is the one for which the devil fell.… Pride is greater than all sins, and the principal sin of the devil.… Often the reason for pride is for him who disregards having an ecclesiastical dignity.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:5

Often having a fullness and an abundance of bread is the cause of arrogance. But often the sin of pride also arises over spiritual gifts, and discernment is needed to distinguish the one from the other.
HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 6:9

But for all this, some are of so senseless a disposition, as even after these words to say, "Nay, far be it from me to weep at any time, but may God grant me to laugh and to play all my days." And what can be more childish than this mind? For it is not God that grants to play, but the devil. At least hear, what was the portion of them that played. "The people," it is said, "sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play." Such were they at Sodom, such were they at the time of the deluge. For touching them of Sodom likewise it is said, that "in pride, and in plenty, and in fullness of bread, they waxed wanton." And they who were in Noah's time, seeing the ark a preparing for so many years, lived on in senseless mirth, foreseeing nought of what was coming. For this cause also the flood came and swept them all away, and wrought in that instant the common shipwreck of the world. Ask not then of God these things, which thou receivest of the devil. For it is God's part to give a contrite and humbled heart, sober, self-possessed, and awestruck, full of repentance and compunction. These are His gifts, forasmuch as it is also of these things that we are most in need.
Commentary on Ezekiel

He therefore who swears and says: As I live, says the Lord, in describing the crimes of Sodom and her daughters, set first pride, which is properly the devil's, and the first sin; hence the same Apostle: Lest, puffed up, he says, with pride, he fall into the judgment of the devil, on account of which he fell from heaven: For he had said: I will make strength and wisdom of understanding, I will take away the boundaries of the nations and lay waste their strength and shake the inhabited cities, and I will seize the whole world with my hand like a nest, and like broken eggs I will carry it off, and: God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble; we read also in another place: Why is earth and ashes proud?; and the Gospel relates the pride of the Pharisee overcome by the humility of the publican; whose seedbed is fullness of bread and abundance of all things and idleness, or, as the Seventy translated, an opulence of delights and luxury; that rich man in the Gospel, clothed in purple, is related to have had no other crime except that, abounding in wealth and riches, he had broken out into such pride that he did not stretch out his hand to the needy and poor Lazarus, and so forgot his own condition that he did not give to the wretched man even what was to be thrown away; for which reason it is also written in another place: Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted. Pride, fullness, abundance of all things, idleness and delights: this is the sin of Sodom, and on account of it there follows forgetfulness of God, which thinks present goods everlasting and that it will never lack necessities; for which reason it is also commanded in the law: Take heed lest, eating and drinking and being filled, having built very fine houses, and having sheep and oxen, silver and gold, you forget the Lord your God, and in another place it is written of Israel: He ate and drank, and was filled and grew fat, and the beloved kicked; knowing which, Solomon too, the wisest of all, prays in Proverbs: Grant me what is necessary and what suffices, lest, being filled, I become a liar and say: Who will see me? or, being made poor, I steal and forswear the name of God.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Furthermore, as to the fact that for 'delights' the Hebrew contains 'idleness', it should be known that it belongs to this sense: every soul of the idle man is in desires; that is, something must always be being done, lest the field of our breast, when the hand ceases, be overrun by the brambles of evil thoughts.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:3
My Lord Jesus Christ is justified according to the dispensation of the flesh that he purified for our salvation, by Abraham, by Isaac, by Jacob and by the rest of the prophets.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 9:3
Before Christ it was not possible for the light of the righteous to shine.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And what follows: And you have justified your sisters in all your abominations which you have wrought, does not declare Sodom and Samaria simply righteous, but by comparison with those who are worse, just as the publican too, of whom we spoke above, is called righteous not absolutely but by comparison with one worse. And yet, though Sodom and Samaria are such, they have not sinned even half, in comparison with Jerusalem: The servant, for, who knows the will of his master and does not do it will be beaten with many stripes, and: The mighty will mightily suffer torments.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 10:1
O you who are subject to pain, do not go into exile with mourning.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 10:1
It is an infamy to be separated from the people of God and from the church; it is a dishonor in the church to leave the bench of presbyters, to be expelled from the rank of the diaconate.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 10:1
If we justify providence, we cleanse our disgrace; but if we do not receive the judgments of God, we will multiply our disgrace.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 10:2
The more we come very near to God the more we come near the beatitude; and when we have sinned, we shall be far from it and very near terrible and very great punishments.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 10:2
The person who is "very small" deserves mercy more quickly.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Therefore you too, bear your shame, you who have surpassed your sisters by your sins, acting more wickedly than they; for they have been justified by you. (LXX: "And you, endure your torment, in that you corrupted your sisters in your sins, by which you acted iniquitously beyond them, and you justified them beyond yourself.") The second plank after shipwreck is, when you have sinned, to blush, and not to fall under that reproach which is spoken against Jerusalem: The face of a harlot has become yours; you do not know how to blush. Now he bears his torment who is tortured by his own conscience, and in this world endures torture of his own will, so that he may not endure eternal torments; and we corrupt our brothers or sisters by our sins when through our sins they are provoked to greater crimes — let what I say be made clearer thus: imagine someone set on the summit of the priesthood not living well and disfiguring his dignity by his works: is not the lay brother corrupted by the imitation of his vices? —; for he too who has scandalized one of the least is cast headlong into the deep with a millstone tied to his neck. The sisters of Jerusalem too, Sodom and Samaria, are justified, not because they are righteous in themselves, but, as we said, in comparison with one who is worse.
Commentary on Ezekiel

Therefore you too, be ashamed and bear your disgrace, you who have justified your sisters. (LXX: "And you, be ashamed and take up your disgrace, because you have justified your sisters.") Shame is followed by disgrace, disgrace by chastisement, chastisement by consolation, consolation by salvation, according to that word of the Apostle: Tribulation works patience, patience proof, proof hope. And hope does not put to shame — no doubt with respect to the future, since in the present it has blotted out its sins through shame —; something of the same kind is sounded by that word of the Gospel too: There is a shame that leads to death, and there is a shame that leads to life; the Holy Spirit too exhorts sinners in the Psalms: Let all my enemies be put to shame and be afraid; let them be turned back, and be put to shame very swiftly; it is written also in another place: Tell your sins first, that you may be justified, and again: The righteous man is his own accuser at the beginning of his speech. It is no wonder, then, if Jerusalem is called to shame and disgrace, she who sinned to such a degree that she justified her sisters, and to whom it is said thereafter: Both you and your daughters, return to your ancient state.
On Lying 5:7

It is one thing to have an action set forth as praiseworthy in itself and another to have it extolled in comparison with something worse than itself. We rejoice in one way when a sick person is cured and in another when he improves a little. Even in the sacred Scriptures, Sodom is spoken of as justified in comparison with the crimes of the people of Israel.
HOMILIES ON EZEKIEL 10:2
Anger is something other than God himself, so that it is never part of him, nor does he share in it in any way.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And I will turn them, restoring them, with the turning of Sodom with her daughters, and with the turning of Samaria and of her daughters; and I will turn your return in the midst of them, that you may bear your disgrace, and you will be ashamed in all that you have done, consoling them. (LXX: "And I will turn their turnings with the turning of Sodom and of her daughters, and I will turn the turning of Samaria and of her daughters; and I will turn your turning in the midst of them, that you may bear your torment, and have disgrace from all that you have done to provoke me to anger.") Great is the progress of Jerusalem, that, after the shame and disgrace brought upon her by the judgment of God, which she willingly accepted and bore, saying: I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, restoration to her ancient state should be promised her. But yet, since by comparison with her crimes Sodom and Samaria were justified, of whom one is on the right and the other on the left, first the 'turning', or 'captivity', of Sodom is restored, as Aquila translated, second the 'captivity' of Samaria, as the same Aquila and Symmachus translated, and last of all Jerusalem is restored, which had been weighed down by greater iniquity and had shown her sinful sisters to be righteous in comparison with herself. For who doubts that among three sinners, nay rather impious men — the Gentile, the heretic, the churchman — he is worthy of much greater punishments who has been of greater dignity? : For the mighty, as we said, will mightily suffer torments; but he who has been least is worthy of mercy, and: The servant who knows the will of his master and does not do it will be beaten with many stripes. Hence Peter too: It is time, he says, for judgment to begin from the house of the Lord; and in this same prophet it is commanded to those who hold axes: Begin from my holy ones, so that Jerusalem last of all, after her sisters have first been turned back and restored to their former state, may bear her disgrace and be ashamed and blush over the things in which she had sinned and in all things console her sisters, while she endures heavier things; or certainly she is ashamed and blushes for this reason, that she provoked God to anger. From which it is plain that anger is not natural to God, but that God, most clement and most gentle, is provoked to anger by our vices, as the Apostle says: Or do you despise the riches of his goodness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that the goodness of God calls you to penance? But according to your hardness and impenitent heart you treasure up wrath for yourself, which the Lord does not have by nature; whence it is also written in another place: You sent forth your wrath, and it devoured them like stubble — for what is joined and united in one body cannot be sent, but only what is outside the body, for example a lance, a javelin, an arrow, a sword —; we read in the Gospel that it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment than for the land that has not received the apostles.
ON FIRST PRINCIPLES 2:5.3

It is plain that the just and good God of the law and the gospels is one and the same and that he does good with justice and punishes in kindness, since neither goodness without justice nor justice without goodness can describe the dignity of the divine nature.
Commentary on Ezekiel

And your sister Sodom and her daughters will return to their antiquity, and Samaria and her daughters will return to their antiquity, and you and your daughters, return to your antiquity. (LXX: "And your sister Sodom and her daughters will be restored as they had been from the beginning, and Samaria and her daughters will be restored as they were from the beginning, and you and your daughters will be restored as you were from the start.") The Jews, among the other fables and endless genealogies and ravings which they invent, dream this too: that at the coming of their Christ, whom we know to be Antichrist, and in the kingdom of a thousand years, Sodom is to be restored to its ancient state, so that it will be like the paradise of God and like the land of Egypt, and that Samaria will receive its former happiness, so that they will return from the Assyrians to the land of Judea — for we read that the ten tribes were taken captive by Pul and Shalmaneser and Tiglath-pileser, kings of the Assyrians, and are captives there to this day —; that Jerusalem too is then to be built, and all her daughters, namely the cities and villages and fortresses that are to be under her power, will flourish as they flourished before, and Jerusalem herself is to be built of gold and silver and precious stones, of which Isaiah too is said to prophesy: I will establish your judges as before and your counselors as from the beginning, and after this you shall be called the city of righteousness, the faithful mother of cities, Zion, and our Revelation to speak, and David to sing: Deal kindly, O Lord, in your good will with Zion, and let the walls of Jerusalem be built, and in another place: The cities of Judea shall be built, and they shall dwell and abide there, and their seed shall be directed forever. But we, leaving the perfect knowledge of these things to the judgment of God, nay rather clearly confessing that after the second coming of the Lord Savior there will be nothing lowly, nothing earthly, but the heavenly kingdoms which are first promised in the Gospel, say this: that in the state of the Church all things have been fulfilled and are fulfilled daily. Sodom returns to its ancient state when the soul, formerly Gentile and impious, restored to its own nature, understands the Creator. Samaria receives her ancient blessedness, the error of the heretics despised, and joined to Christian doctrine and faith. And when they have returned, Jerusalem too, 'vision of peace', which is interpreted as the Church, will return to her former state — of which it is written: His place has been made in peace, and: Jerusalem, which is built as a city whose sharing thereof is in the selfsame, and in the Apostle: But the Jerusalem which is above is free, which is our mother, and in the same: You have come to Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and thousands of angels in throngs —, and she will return with her daughters, who are scattered over the whole world; of which we have treated more fully in the explanations of Isaiah.
Commentary on Ezekiel

But Sodom your sister was not heard in your mouth in the day of your pride, before your wickedness was uncovered, as at this time, to the reproach of the daughters of Syria, and of all the Palestinian daughters round about you, who surround you on every side. Your crime and your disgrace you have borne, says the Lord God. (LXX: "If Sodom your sister had not been for hearing in your mouth in the days of your pride, before your wickednesses were uncovered, as now is the case with the daughters of Syria, and if this had not been, what would have been done to you, and to all round about you, the daughters of the foreigners who surround you on every side? Your impieties and your iniquities, you, bear them.") Symmachus translated this passage thus: Because Sodom your sister was not in hearing through your mouth in the day of your pride, before your disgrace was uncovered, as in the time of the reproach of the daughters of Syria, and of all the Palestinian daughters who are round about you, who surround you on every side.
